headline: Braves rally in eighth, ninth to edge Phillies 5-4
recap: The Braves beat the Phillies 5-4 at Citizens Bank Park on Sunday, taking the third game of their four-game series. Philadelphia led 2-0 after the first: Luis Arraez's sacrifice fly scored Kyle Schwarber, and Alec Bohm's double drove in Trea Turner. Atlanta got a run back in the sixth on Ronald Acuña Jr.'s sacrifice fly, but Derek Hill and Schwarber both homered in the bottom of the seventh, Schwarber's the 42nd of his season, to put the Phillies up 4-1. The Braves tied it in the eighth when Acuña's three-run homer, his 16th, came off reliever Alex McFarlane, and Austin Riley's triple in the ninth off Jhoan Duran brought home the go-ahead run. Aaron Nola allowed one run over seven innings with five strikeouts and did not factor in the decision. Dylan Lee got the win, Raisel Iglesias picked up his 31st save, and Duran (2-5) took the loss.

The loss dropped Philadelphia to 80-63, second in the NL East, five games behind Atlanta, and snapped a one-game winning streak. The Phillies hold the second National League wild card position, 4.5 games ahead of the cutoff.

Philadelphia and Atlanta close out the series Monday afternoon at Citizens Bank Park, with Jesús Luzardo starting for the Phillies opposite the Braves' Grant Holmes. First pitch is scheduled for 1:05 PM ET. DraftKings has the Phillies favored at -168, with Philadelphia at -1.5 on the run line (+128).
